column1: # The species built by reactome.py. This is the only place the species list lives.
# Nothing reads this file positionally except load_species(), so a new column may
# be inserted anywhere. (build/manifest.tsv is the opposite: the workflow slices
# it with cut/read, so columns there may only be appended.)
# code              names input_<code>.txt, config/reactome_<code>.config, reactome_<code>.xgmml
# reactome_species  species exactly as spelled in NCBI2Reactome.txt column 6
# ncbi_token        names <ncbi_token>.gene_info.gz at NCBI; not derivable from the
#                   Reactome spelling, which uses a space rather than an underscore
# ncbi_clade        directory under ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/DATA/GENE_INFO/
# bridgedb_species  species key in bridgedb/data gene.json
# syscodes_out      BridgeDb systems to expand gene ids into; H (HGNC) is human-only
# tier              core = too few pathways fails the run; extra = skipped; off = not built
# min_mapped_frac   QC floor for BridgeDb cross-reference coverage
# max_reject_frac   ceiling on genes dropped for having no NCBI symbol (human is 3.6%)
# code

# The other eleven buildable species are held back pending a decision on whether
# orthology-inferred pathways belong in a linkset. Reactome projects most
# non-human content from human by orthology: all 1467 mouse pathways share both
# their name and their numeric stem with a human pathway, and R-MMU-73843 reports
# isInferred. Rat, cow, dog, zebrafish, pig, Xenopus and C. elegans are likewise
# 100% IEA. Fly, chicken and yeast are NOT -- 74 Drosophila, 39 Gallus and 1
# S. cerevisiae pathways are curated (TAS) with no human stem -- so enabling them
# is a per-species judgement, not one switch.
# Enabling any of these also needs its .bridge bundle cached: update-bridgedb.yml
# reads wikipathways/species.tsv, so xtr and ssc would have to be added there too.
